item.title: Manhattan DA's office says Luigi Mangione defense spread false claims about murder trial media plan
item.description: Prosecutors accuse Luigi Mangione's defense team of spreading misinformation about media access plans for his upcoming Manhattan murder trial.
item.content:encoded:
Manhattan prosecutors asked a judge Monday to correct what they called false claims by Luigi Mangione's defense team about media access to his upcoming murder trial and remind the attorneys of their ethical obligations.

The filing came days after Mangione's lawyers argued the court's plan for public and media access violates his constitutional right to a public trial and alleged the Manhattan District Attorney's Office was involved in deciding which reporters would be allowed to cover the proceedings.

Prosecutors denied the allegation, saying the office "had no role" in developing the New York State Office of Court Administration's media access plan or selecting journalists to cover the trial.

MANGIONE LAWYERS SAY MEDIA LIMITS AT MURDER TRIAL ARE UNCONSTITUTIONAL, FEAR COURT WILL 'HAND-PICK' PRESS

"The defense's baseless accusation thus appears to be nothing more than an attempt to spread misinformation about this case and delegitimize the proceedings," Senior Trial Counsel Joel J. Seidemann wrote in a letter to Judge Gregory Carro.

The Manhattan District Attorney's Office asked Carro to remind Mangione's attorneys of their ethical obligations not to knowingly make false statements to a court or third parties, citing New York's Rules of Professional Conduct.

FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X

In Friday's filing, defense attorneys Karen Friedman Agnifilo, Marc Agnifilo and Jacob Kaplan argued the court's media access restrictions amount to a partial closure of the proceedings in violation of the First, Sixth and Fourteenth Amendments.

TYLER ROBINSON ASKS FOR MORE SECRET HEARINGS AFTER LOSING FIGHT OVER CAMERAS IN COURT

The attorneys objected to the lack of an overflow courtroom, limits on jury selection coverage and what they described as a process allowing only a select group of reporters to attend the trial.

LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST

They also claimed they were told only 68 journalists would receive general access to the proceedings and that the selection process had effectively been outsourced to a private attorney representing several legacy media organizations.

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS

Mangione's attorneys asked the court to hold a public hearing, identify the journalists selected to cover jury selection and the broader trial, explain how those reporters were chosen and detail efforts to secure an overflow courtroom.

GOT A TIP?

They also asked the court to either broadcast the proceedings live or explain why that would not be permitted.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE

Prosecutors responded Monday that the defense had wrongly implicated the district attorney's office in decisions made by the Office of Court Administration.

GET BREAKING NEWS BY EMAIL

"The District Attorney's Office had no role in developing the Office of Court Administration's media access plan for this trial, and will have no role in selecting which news reporters attend the trial, as defense counsel surely knows from her long prior association with this office," Seidemann wrote in the filing.

Fox News Digital has reached out to Friedman Agnifilo and Mangione's spokesperson for comment on the matter.

Mangione is charged in New York state court with murder and terrorism-related offenses in the Dec. 4, 2024, fatal shooting of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson outside a Manhattan hotel. He has pleaded not guilty.

item.title: HEAR IT: Mom's frantic 911 call after thief steals Instacart driver's car with toddler inside
item.description: Body camera video and 911 audio reveal the frantic 15-minute rescue of a 2-year-old from a stolen car during an Instacart delivery in Atlanta.
item.content:encoded:
A routine Instacart delivery turned into every parent's nightmare after a Georgia mother's car was stolen with her 2-year-old daughter still inside, as newly released 911 audio and police body camera video capture the frantic rescue.

"Someone just stole my car and it has my 2-year-old daughter in it," the distraught mother tells an Atlanta 911 dispatcher in audio released by police.

When the dispatcher asks whether the child is inside the vehicle, the mother replies, "Yes, my 2-year-old daughter was in the backseat. I was dropping off an Instacart order and I came back outside and my car is gone. My daughter was inside."

HELICOPTER FOOTAGE CAPTURES FLORIDA MAN ALLEGEDLY ABANDONING CHILD DURING HIGH-SPEED CHASE FROM DEPUTIES

Moments later, she cries out again, "My daughter was inside!"

The ordeal unfolded around 4:36 p.m. on July 30, according to the Atlanta Police Department.

Police said the vehicle had been left running with the toddler inside while her mother delivered an Instacart order.

LICENSE PLATE CAMERAS ARE TRACKING DRIVERS EVERYWHERE

Officers with the department's Auto Crimes Enforcement Unit immediately began searching for the vehicle and used the city's license plate readers to locate the car, the suspect and the child in under 15 minutes, according to police.

Body camera video released by the department shows officers surrounding the stolen vehicle and ordering the driver to raise his hands and get out.

"Hands up! Hands up!" an officer shouts.

MIKE WALTZ, TIM TEBOW LAUNCH EFFORT TO COMBAT ONLINE CHILD EXPLOITATION: 'IT'S HAPPENING IN THEIR BACKYARD'

"Hands on the window now," another officer orders. "What you're gonna do is you're going to get out and face away from me, you understand me? Get out the car, slow. Put your hands behind your back."

The video shows officers taking the suspect into custody as the toddler cries nearby and her mother works to calm her.

"It's okay, baby. It's okay, baby," the mother can be heard saying.

Moments later, an officer radios, "The child is okay. The child's okay."

Police identified the suspect as 21-year-old Saleem Martin.

Martin was charged with kidnapping, theft by taking, simple battery, entering an automobile, cruelty to children and criminal attempt to commit a felony, according to police.

Authorities said the toddler was unharmed and reunited with her parents.

According to an arrest warrant obtained by Atlanta NBC affiliate 11Alive, the child's mother later noticed that the bottom of her daughter's dress was unbuttoned.

The warrant alleges the toddler told her mother "the man did it," referring to the man who had been driving the car.

Martin allegedly had both hands on the child's torso when officers found him and was trying to duck down and hide between the seats, according to the warrant cited by the outlet.

The Atlanta Police Department's Special Victims Unit was brought into the investigation.

Martin allegedly told investigators he had been touching the child because he was trying to calm her down, according to 11Alive.

He also allegedly claimed he jumped into the vehicle because he was trying to "get back to New Jersey" and did not realize the toddler was in the backseat until after he drove away.

According to the arrest warrant, Martin also allegedly told investigators he realized there was an iPad inside the vehicle and discarded it because he believed it could be used to track him.

Fox News Digital reached out to the Atlanta Police Department for comment.

item.title: Nick Saban's assistants had a system for sneaking onto golf courses without him knowing, until it backfired
item.description: Steve Sarkisian drained a hole-in-one while hiding from Nick Saban on a Tuscaloosa golf course during spring practice, and word traveled fast.
item.content:encoded:
No matter where his assistant coaches went while at Alabama, former coach Nick Saban always had a watchful eye on his staff members who would sneak out of the office for a round of golf.

In Tuscaloosa, there were plenty of interesting stories to come out regarding Saban assistants finding time to get out of the office in the offseason.

College football is finally back after months of NCAA lawsuits, NIL drama and congressional fights

Whether it was scrambling to get a round of basketball in during their 'free time' or trying to decipher which golf course within driving range of Alabama's campus that Nick Saban was heading to for a round was all part of the game.

For Ole Miss head coach Pete Golding, there was a method to their madness, and it involved getting a tip from whomever Saban was golfing with that day.

Whichever course Saban went to, the assistants would head to the other one in town. That worked, until the now Rebels coach had a breakdown in communication on where their boss was actually at.

"There are two courses in Tuscaloosa. You got Indian Hills and you got North River," Pete Golding explained. "I was told that coach Saban was playing North River. So, I got our group together and said 'hey, let's go to to Indian Hills' during the day at like 2 o'clock. Sometimes in the spring after lunch, coach (Saban) would disappear. You wouldn’t know, he didn’t tell ya.

LANE KIFFIN CAN'T STOP TALKING ABOUT OLE MISS, EVEN WHILE EXPLAINING WHY HE CHOSE LSU OVER FLORIDA

"Well, we're on 10, which is a Par-3 over the water and sixteen is coming back in this direction. We got Stoops, Sarkisian and Freddie Roach. So, Sark is about to tee-off and we look down on sixteen green, and there's coach Saban with the Pro at Indian Hills and two of his buddies."

Ok, well right then Golding had to know the jig was up.

The Alabama assistant coach and his co-workers should have probably called it a day. But, given that they were already on the course, and their boss was down the fairway on another hole, the foursome decided to risk it.

Unfortunately, this would turn out to be one of the craziest experiences for the assistant coaches, thanks to a shot from now Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian.

"We're deciding should we hit or not, and Sark is like we'll just be quiet and hit," Golding recalled. "He hits like 145 or whatever, with an eight-iron. He hits it, then it hits like one time and goes in the hole. A hole-in-one. It's like you're watching a movie in mute. Nobody wants to say anything, because we can't let Saban know.

"The pro over there sees it and asks 'who hit that'. We bee-lined straight for the carts, like nobody else even hits and we're down there hiding in the woods or whatever."

In case you were wondering, it did not take long for coach Nick Saban to find out about the insane hole-in-one from his assistant coach, Steve Sarkisian. If you've never been to Tuscaloosa, I promise you that word travels fast, especially on the golf course.

"We hear about it the next day. He ain't gonna sit around and come over there and make it awkward."

Imagine that. Hitting a fantastic shot, knowing that the strictest coach in college football is standing just over on the next green, and you cannot celebrate the shot.

This actually makes the entire afternoon that much better, at least in my eyes.

Nick Saban is known for being a competitor on the course, so figuring out that Steve Sarkisian drained a hole-in-one while the staff was supposed to be back at the office breaking down film during the spring undoubtedly had the former Alabama coach looking for answers.

And, it wouldn’t take him long to find out who hit the shot.

I think we've all heard the stories of what it was like working for Nick Saban as an assistant coach at any one of his stops as a head coach.

But, deciding to still move forward with their round of golf knowing the boss would find out at some point took fortitude.

Now, imagine the other stories that could be told from Saban's time at Alabama.

item.title: Michigan's Democratic AG refuses to attend upcoming convention over harassment concerns
item.description: Michigan Attorney General Dana Nessel said she won't attend the Michigan Democratic Party convention in August, citing fears of harassment and antisemitism.
item.content:encoded:
Michigan Attorney General Dana Nessel told Jewish leaders and community members during a roundtable last week that she has no plans to attend the Michigan Democratic Party’s nominating convention next month out of concern for her safety.

"I feel like my presence isn’t going to be welcome," Nessel said, according to the Michigan Advance. "I don’t want to get chased around. I don’t want to get harassed. I don’t want to get yelled and screamed at. I don’t want to get booed off the stage, irrespective of what I’m saying. And I believe that if I go, that is what will happen because it’s been happening to me."

Nessel, the first Jewish person to be elected Michigan's attorney general, claimed that party leadership has neglected her concerns over the rise of antisemitism within the Democratic Party despite reporting that she was harassed by some members.

Michigan Democratic Jewish Caucus chair Jessica Alexander told Fox News Digital that she respected Nessel's decision and, though she does not believe that the Democratic Party itself is antisemitic, acknowledged a rise in "anti-Jewish" attitudes among dissenters. 

LEFT-WING ACTIVISTS HECKLE PRO-ISRAEL DEMOCRAT HALEY STEVENS AT MICHIGAN CONVENTION

"At this point, why should she put herself in a circumstance that feels untenable and reactionary? As active and dedicated members, we don't feel or believe the Democratic Party is antisemitic, but the anti-AIPAC rhetoric circling many current campaigns is a dog whistle for classic anti-Jewish tropes such as ‘Jews hold the power, they have the money, rising gas prices are their fault, etc.,’" Alexander said.

Alexander, who is a professor at Eastern Michigan University, added that as someone not "open to immense scrutiny" like an elected official, she is planning on attending the convention, expecting a "large turnout" for her caucus. 

Nessel said she could say as a Democrat that "some things have changed," according to the Advance, and that society had to exist where "intelligent discourse and debate" could occur without threats.

Fox News Digital reached out to the Michigan Democratic Party for comment.

BILL MAHER OFFERS A STARK WARNING FOR DEMOCRATS CODDLING ANTISEMITES, CALLS OUT ‘WOKE IDIOTS’ IN THE PARTY

A spokesperson for the Michigan Democratic Party told the Michigan Advance that the party rejects "antisemitism, Islamophobia, and all forms of hateful conduct" and that the organization is "ensuring party-hosted events are safe and secure environments for all attendees" at the Aug. 29 convention.

Nessel revealed in 2023 that she was the target of a "heavily armed defendant" who was allegedly plotting attacks against Jewish elected officials in the wake of Israel's war in Gaza.

She also clashed with progressive "Squad" member Rep. Rashida Tlaib, D-Mich., after bringing charges against anti-Israel protesters at the University of Michigan.

BATYA UNGAR-SARGON EXPLAINS WHY SO MANY AMERICAN JEWS BECAME DEMS — AND WHY SOME NOW FEEL POLITICALLY HOMELESS

Nessel is far from the only Michigan Democrat to express concerns over antisemitism within her party. Former Senate candidate Mallory McMorrow confirmed during a debate in May before she suspended her campaign that disdain for Jewish people among Democrats is a growing problem.

"At the Democratic convention, an attendee yelled an antisemitic slur at my husband, who is Jewish and was walking with my 5-year-old daughter. That is terrifying," McMorrow said.

Some Jewish Democrats have also reported intending to vote for Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers if progressive candidate Abdul El-Sayed wins the upcoming Democratic primary.

item.title: Maggie Sajak is ashamed of her Dodgers, baseball player throws a punch during a pickle & ESPN's trans drooling
item.description: Tarik Skubal's trade to the Dodgers has fans fuming and demanding a salary cap as the MLB trade deadline fuels serious lockout fears this winter.
item.content:encoded:
'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday–Friday on OutKick.com.

Happy MLB Trade Deadline day to all who celebrate!

Sure, I know that's a niche topic, but man — there is nothing better than a trade deadline day in sports. Any sport, really. Take your pick.

The NFL trade deadline in October used to be a waste of time, but not anymore. The baseball deadline has always been electric, and this year is no different.

In fact, people are on edge from coast to coast right now because of the Tarik Skubal trade over the weekend. Did you hear about that?

SENDING ACE PITCHER TARIK SKUBAL TO THE LOS ANGELES DODGERS WOULD OFFICIALLY RUIN BASEBALL

Of course you did! Fans are FUMING right now. Folks are ready to lock it down. They want a salary cap. They want the Dodgers relegated forever. Even LA fans are walking on eggshells.

Speaking of ... welcome to a Monday Nightcaps — the one where Maggie Sajak bleeds Dodger blue in secrecy as baseball barrels towards a lost season. We'll get into it.

What else? I've got a Mexican League player sucker punching a third baseman during a rundown (seriously), ESPN Radio bringing back Mike Golic out of nowhere, and how about the insane gushing by the World Wide (Woke) Leader over the Minnesota coach yesterday?

My God. These people are just nuts. It's amazing.

OK, grab you a chocolate chip cookie for National Chocolate Chip Cookie Day, and settle in for a Monday 'Cap!

My wife made some sort of healthy, chickpea/almond flour/protein powder chocolate chip cookies today for the kids, and they were good. Fair is fair, and they got the job done. MAHA Mom!

That being said, the healthy stuff doesn't hold a candle to the old school ingredients. Not even close.

Mount Rushmore of Cookies? Sure, why not? It's the first Monday of August, after all.

1. Heath Bar (the ones from Publix deserve to be in the Hall of Fame)

2. Sugar (needs to be soft and a little doughy, though)

3. Peanut Butter (see above)

4. Oatmeal Raisin (probably won't be popular but that doesn't mean it's wrong)

There you have it. You are welcome! Another great Ted Talk in the books to start August.

Now, let's get this class started by checking in with Maggie Sajak and the LA Dodgers, who are officially the most villainous team in sports since ... the '90s Yankees?

Does Maggie speak for all Dodgers fans today? Are you embarrassed by your team?

Look, I'm not Dodger fan. I'm actually a Red Sox fan, which has been just incredible over the past six weeks. 28-5 since June 26! Just amazing.

Anyway, I don't blame the Dodgers. Some folks are furious with them today. Everyone is convinced they're ruining baseball and pushing us towards a lockout this winter.

That may be the case, but the Skubal trade has nothing to do with it. Literally any team in baseball could A) afford to have taken on Skubal's $9 million salary for the rest of this year, and B) put together a package to match what the Dodgers gave up ...

... mainly because it was a pretty crappy package.

So, why were the Dodgers the only team to step up to the plate? Or, better yet, why did the Tigers jump at that trade? I have no clue, but I do have a conspiracy theory.

The rabbit hole in me thinks the rest of the owners allowed the Dodgers to make this trade because they want the public on their side during these upcoming negotiations. They were thinking long term.

These lockouts are always about perception. It dictates everything, and it's usually on the players' side.

This looming lockout — and there will 100% be a lockout — could be the first time in history where the fans side with the owners.

Regardless, don't blame the Dodgers for picking up the phone and making the call. They gave up peanuts for a two-time Cy Young award winner. Every other team could've done it, and they chose not to.

At least the LA faithful packed the stadium yesterday to show their appreciation!

Lordy. Look at that stadium! It was half-empty for a Sunday afternoon game against the Red Sox! Boots on the ground tell me that a bunch of fans didn't show up because it was "hot" and "sunny."

Give me a break. Hilarious.

OK, let's leave LA and head across the border, where Mexican League outfielder Danry Vasquez punched his way out of a pickle this weekend:

Whoaaaaaaaaaaa Nellie! I've been in baseball for a long time now — as a player and now a Big J writer — and I can confidently say that I've never seen someone do that. What a brawl.

And how about the shot Vasquez took after landing the initial punch? Just gets pummeled from behind. Absolute beatdown.

Now, peeling back the curtain a bit here, I'd normally go into a long diatribe breaking this fight down — punch by punch. I'd have some fun with it.

BUT, some digging showed me that this Danry Vasquez is an absolute scumbag and has done some really disgusting things in the past. Yes, there is video. Yes, it involved his girlfriend. No, I will not be showing it here.

You can find it on your own if you'd like, it's not hard. It's a tough watch. I'd suggest you just take my word for it.

Seems like this guy shouldn't ever be allowed near a baseball field again.

OK, let's rapid-fire this Monday class into a big Monday night of trading! First up? I can't get over the wokes over at ESPN gushing over the Lynx coach wearing a 'protect trans kids' shirt during yesterday's game:

SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM TAKES VICIOUS ELBOW TO FACE, AND FANS FUME AT WHAT REFS DID NEXT

"I would encourage to go and listen to Cheryl Reeve's comments."

Yeah, no ... we're good. Thanks, though, ESPN! And how about the stones on Cheryl giving Sophie Cunningham a lecture before the game?

What did Trump say during his SOTU earlier this year?

"These people are CRAZY."

They really are. Just insane.

Speaking of ESPN ... anyone notice who was back on the FM/AM airwaves this morning?

Mike Golic! Wow. What a throwback. I hadn't heard Golic on ESPN in a decade. Lordy, do I miss those days.

I can vividly remember waking up every day at the crack of dawn and going to school in the old 1997 jeep wrangler with the top down and listening to a static "Mike & Mike" on AM radio. It was a staple in our car for years. Then we'd get Cowherd on the drive home.

Perhaps this is the latest sign that ESPN is moving back to that era? I hope so, but I'll believe it when I see it.

After all, we did have an announcer treating Cheryl Reeves wearing a pro-trans shirt like the falling of the Berlin wall just 24 hours ago, so I won't be holding my breath.

OK, that's it for today. Good start to the week. Good start to August.

Here's an old broadcast of the night that Yankees great Thurman Munson died to take us into the week.

Incredible scene.

RIP!

Are the Dodgers to blame for the Skubal trade? Email me at Zach.Dean@OutKick.com.

item.title: Phil Collins' brush with death left his children preparing for the unthinkable
item.description: Phil Collins reveals his children were called to say goodbye while he lay unconscious in a Swiss hospital with organs shutting down from alcoholism.
item.content:encoded:
Phil Collins' biggest heartbreak didn't happen onstage.

The music icon revealed the emotional goodbye he shared with his children in 2024 while facing life-threatening health struggles and alcoholism, unsure if he would make it home. Collins' manager called up the singer's five children — Lily, Joely, Simon, Nicolas and Matthew — while he lay unconscious in a Swiss hospital.

"Because there were some decisions to be made about ‘Do we keep Phil on life support?’ kind of thing," he told The Sunday Times.

RANDY TRAVIS' HEALTH CRISIS BEGAN WITH 'CONGESTION' AND ENDED IN A FIVE-MONTH HOSPITAL STAY

"My kidneys were packing up, my organs were just seizing up," Collins explained. "People were coming to say goodbye."

While Collins has little memory of those harrowing days, his children carried the weight of believing they could be saying their final goodbyes.

"But I don’t remember them coming," he admitted. "I didn’t have no idea this was going on. They were all worried that they wouldn’t see me again. It could all have gone so terribly wrong."

IS DRINKING EVERY DAY ALCOHOLISM? EXPERTS EXPLAIN WHERE CULTURE AND ADDICTION COLLIDE

Surviving the ordeal prompted Collins to make a life-changing decision about his drinking.

"I was very lucky to have come out of that," Collins told the publication, adding, "Needless to say, I haven’t had a drink since."

Months later, Collins spent time reconnecting with his kids after surviving the frightening brush with death. Lily "was sitting beside me in tears, saying, ‘I never thought I’d get these moments,'" he recalled.

"We had an incredible time," he added. "I can’t overemphasize how fantastic it was."

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

His health issues didn't disappear. Collins revealed it's an "ongoing thing" during an appearance on the BBC podcast "Eras" earlier this year.

"I have a 24-hour, live-in nurse to make sure I take my medication as I should do," he explained. "I’ve had challenges with my knee. I had everything that could go wrong with me, did go wrong with me."

Collins has long been candid about the personal battles that accompanied his declining health, including his yearslong struggle with alcoholism. 

He built a Hall of Fame career as both the drummer and later lead singer of Genesis before becoming a global solo superstar in the 1980s.

As a solo artist, he sold more than 100 million records worldwide with hits including "In the Air Tonight," "Against All Odds," "Sussudio," "One More Night" and "Another Day in Paradise."

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Collins wrote about his struggle with alcoholism in his 2016 autobiography, "Not Dead Yet."

"Night after night I find myself lying on the bed, staring out of a skylight at grey Swiss skies, rueing my life," he wrote, according to People. "I’m all alone, save for my good friends Johnnie Walker and Grey Goose. ‘You’ve got everything,’ I think, ‘but you’ve really got f--k all.'"

Collins didn't shy away from describing how quickly his life unraveled after retirement.

"It took me until the age of 55 to become an alcoholic," he wrote. "I got through the heady Sixties, the trippy Seventies, the imperial Eighties, the busy Nineties. I was retired, content – then I fell. Because suddenly, I had too much time on my hands."

"The huge hole, the void, I had to fill somehow," Collins added. "I filled it with booze. And it nearly killed me."

item.title: Renewed patriotism and career opportunities fuel Army's biggest recruiting surge in years
item.description: Retention and recruiting goals are being exceeded as young Americans pursue Army careers in engineering, military intelligence and helicopter mechanics.
item.content:encoded:
The U.S. Army has already reached its fiscal year 2026 active-duty recruiting goal months ahead of schedule, marking a dramatic turnaround after years of falling short as military leaders point to renewed patriotism, career opportunities and a growing sense of purpose among young Americans choosing to serve.

Fox News was granted exclusive access inside Fort Hood, one of the Army’s largest installations, where commanders and soldiers offered a firsthand look at what they say is driving the recruiting resurgence.

Just a few years ago, the Army was struggling to meet its recruiting goals. After hitting a low in fiscal year 2022, recruiting has climbed every year since, rising nearly 38% overall, with the biggest jump coming in fiscal year 2025. This fiscal year, the Army has already met its active-duty recruiting goal with more than 61,500 future soldiers signing on for service.

FIRST ON FOX: TRUMP TO OPEN DIRECT LINE WITH MILITARY FAMILIES IN GROUND-UP READINESS PUSH

The recruiting surge has been accompanied by another encouraging trend for Army leaders: retention goals are also being exceeded, with more soldiers choosing to continue their military careers.

Among them is infantryman Guadalupe Campos, who joined the Army when he was 18 years old and recently extended his service nearly six years later.

"I wanted to do my due diligence and service to my country," Campos told Fox News.

TRUMP GIVES EMOTIONAL TRIBUTE TO FALLEN ARMY LT TYLER FEEHAN AFTER FLYING GRIEVING FAMILY ON AIR FORCE ONE

For Campos, serving in uniform has reinforced both his patriotism and the bonds formed alongside fellow soldiers.

"I love my country, I love America. This is our home, and we have, I mean, this is everything that we all have in common is this American flag that we fly on our right shoulder," he said.

Campos said the Army brought together people from every walk of life, united by one common mission.

TRUMP IS PROVING THAT THE WAY TO BETTER OUR MILITARY IS TO SECURE OUR SUPPLY CHAINS

"A lot of the guys that I worked with, they come from a lot of parts of life, whether it’s good or bad. And at the end of the day, we have that one common goal and that’s to be ready when the time comes for us to have to do our jobs," he said. "We serve and protect the United States Constitution and its people from enemies of a foreign and domestic, and we take that to heart."

Jade Root, Army Recruiting battalion commander, said the recent turnaround reflects a broader desire among young Americans to serve.

"Locally we have seen a strong sense of young men and women who want to serve a purpose much higher than themselves. They understand the opportunities that the Army provides to acquire critical skills and leadership skills that will last them a lifetime," Root told Fox News.

Root also believes the recruiting numbers reflect something larger.

"I think it shows a strong signal that patriotism is alive and well," Rood said. "We have a high propensity of people that want to serve, but most importantly that our Army is growing."

Army leaders say today’s recruits are motivated by a combination of patriotism, benefits and a sense of purpose.

The Army says today’s typical recruit is about 23 years old, and recruiters are spending more time in high schools, on college campuses and in local communities to connect with potential future soldiers.

"I always ask our recruiters, remember they are not just a number, this is someone’s son or daughter," Root said.

Today’s Army also extends far beyond traditional combat roles, offering more than 200 career fields, ranging from medics and helicopter mechanics to cybersecurity, engineering, military intelligence and animal care.

Army Animal Care Specialist Grizel Cornejo said many prospective recruits are surprised by the range of career opportunities available while serving.

FOLLOW US ON X

"It's really encouraging for people to realize they can have the career they want… but also be in the Army and serve the country," Cornejo said.

As modern warfare continues to evolve, Army leaders say they’re increasingly looking for recruits with technical skills in areas such as cybersecurity, engineering and military intelligence as the service prepares for the future battlefield.

For commanders at Fort Hood, the recruiting rebound is about more than reaching a numerical goal. They say it reflects a new generation stepping forward to serve, one motivated by patriotism, opportunity and a willingness to answer the call.

item.title: Baserunner sparks brawl in Mexican Baseball League after sucker punching a fielder who tagged him out
item.description: Danry Vasquez punched and kicked a third baseman after a routine tag, sparking a massive Mexican Baseball League brawl that sent a player out by ambulance.
item.content:encoded:
Chaos broke out in the fourth inning of Sunday night's Liga Mexicana de Béisbol, aka Mexican Baseball League, game between the Toros de Tijuana and the Acereros de Monclova.

A runner ended up in the pickle after trying to score on a ground ball to third that wasn't fielded cleanly. He didn’t end up scoring and was tagged out on the play by the third baseman.

The runner, Tijuana's Danry Vasquez, a noted scumbag with a violent past who spent time in a couple of Major League Baseball organizations, responded to being tagged out on the play by throwing punches.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON’T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

By noted scumbag, I mean he was arrested and charged with domestic violence for an assault on his then-girlfriend in the stairwell of Whataburger Field that resulted in the Houston Astros releasing him.

Back to this insane play. The tag appeared to be of the normal everyday variety. Certainly nothing worthy of the response it was met with.

After hitting Monclova third baseman Rodolfo Amador in the back, Vasquez dropped him with a right hand to the face. Both benches cleared, and all hell broke loose.

MLB DROPS HAMMER ON BOSTON'S WILLSON CONTRERAS WITH HEFTY SUSPENSION AFTER HELMET-THROWING INCIDENT

Before the action, which started on the third baseline, moved towards the mound, Vasquez can be seen kicking Amador while he was still down on the ground.

Vasquez was then knocked to the ground himself as he backpedaled by a justifiable clothesline from Monclova first baseman Ryan Hernandez.

item.title: Eagles' Nolan Smith took apology for his 136 MPH driving arrest to team ownership and now makes it public

item.content:encoded:
Nolan Smith's brush with the law this offseason led the Philadelphia Eagles linebacker on something of an apology tour but while he's in the clear with the team, his status under the NFL's Personal Conduct Policy remains unclear.

Smith was arrested in May after he was stopped by the Twiggs County Sheriff's Office on charges of for allegedly driving his 2026 Lamborghini at 136 MPH in a 70-MPH stretch of Interstate 16 in Twiggs County, Georgia.

Just a very fast car learning a very expensive lesson."

Smith was cited for speeding and reckless driving.

The Eagles didn't love this and Smith said he was sorry.

He took that apology public on Monday when he spoke of the incident for the first time.

"I apologized to the organization and, um, I'll make that apology now, you know?" Smith told reporters on Monday. "I represent the Eagles no matter where I go. You know, Georgia, Florida. It doesn't matter.

The Eagles obviously accepted Smith's apology as he remains on the roster, is expected to get significant snaps from his linebacker spot, and is tied contractually to the team through the 2027 season.

item.title: Netflix replaces fan-favorite football host with unpopular, far-left personality
item.description: Netflix named Elle Duncan as its lead NFL studio host, replacing fan-favorite Kay Adams for the Week 1 49ers vs. Rams broadcast from Australia.
item.content:encoded:
Netflix has replaced Kay Adams with former ESPN host Elle Duncan as its lead NFL studio host for the upcoming season.

On Monday, the streamer announced its studio team for the Week 1 broadcast on Sept. 10, when it will exclusively stream the 49ers vs. Rams from Melbourne, Australia. Duncan will host alongside desk analysts Michael Irvin, Nick Foles, and Clay Matthews.

While Netflix signed Duncan earlier this year to be the face of its sports division, there was at least some question about whether she'd also take over NFL hosting responsibilities, a role Adams held the past two seasons.

The decision is also questionable.

Kay Adams is a fan favorite and one of the best NFL hosts in the industry. If a network with NFL rights were building for the future, it'd likely rank Adams second only to ESPN's Laura Rutledge as its ideal lead host.

By contrast, Duncan is a toxic figure. She is best known at ESPN for reportedly convincing executives that Sage Steele was "not black enough" to participate in a social justice special, protesting Florida's "Don't Say Gay" law live on ESPN, and encouraging fathers to support their daughters' abortions from the SportsCenter set.

USA TODAY REPORTER APOLOGIZES FOR INVOKING EMMETT TILL IN COLUMN ABOUT CAITLIN CLARK AFTER UPSETTING THE WOKE

Last week, Duncan blamed Caitlin Clark and her fans for the ongoing turmoil surrounding the WNBA, just days after USA Today shamefully suggested Clark's on-court antics could lead to the lynching of Black people.

Duncan then criticized Clark for not telling fans not to "use her name" to spread hate, despite Clark doing exactly that.

"People should not be using my name to push those agendas. It's disappointing. It's not acceptable," Clark said in 2024. "Treating every single woman in this league with the same amount of respect, I think, it's just a basic human thing that everybody should do."

Notice Duncan hasn't called on Angel Reese to condemn those using her name to justify similar bigotry, namely the racially charged attacks directed at Clark and her fans.

Duncan is a bad-faith actress. She is dishonest. And her presence on Netflix inevitably politicizes the broadcast.

Netflix has already faced deserved criticism for its sports coverage, often turning live events into infomercials for its entertainment division.

ELLE DUNCAN BLAMES CAITLIN CLARK, HER FANS FOR MEDIA SMEAR CAMPAIGN WHILE IGNORING FACTS

Longtime sports radio host Dan Patrick criticized the company's approach during the Home Run Derby last month.

"I'd like to think I'm at least socially aware of sporting events, but I had no idea," Patrick said. "And then all of a sudden, it's like Netflix, and then you had Will Ferrell show up, you had Bonds and Pujols, and I'm like, OK. They're trying. Netflix is trying, trying different things. Now, sometimes you can try too hard. Sometimes you can try to dress something up, and you really don't need to."

Adams, at least, kept the focus on football, a sport she has covered for years. Duncan has little connection to the leagues Netflix carries, namely the NFL and MLB.

Fans will already be annoyed that they need yet another streaming service to watch Week 1 of the NFL season. Wait until they finally log in and hear Duncan screeching, probably about the fact that the Rams-49ers game features two White quarterbacks and head coaches.

Yes, she is one of those.

Adams is a good football host. Replacing her with Duncan raises questions about how much merit and audience preference factor into Netflix's programming decisions.

We suspect not much.

item.title: Tourist hot spot slapped with US travel warning renewal due to crime and terror
item.description: The U.S. State Department warns travelers of petty crime, pickpocketing and terrorism risks in Belgium, urging Americans to stay alert in popular tourist areas.
item.content:encoded:
Americans traveling to Belgium are facing a renewed travel warning from the U.S. State Department after officials cited concerns about crime, terrorism and civil unrest.

The department recently increased Belgium's advisory to Level 2, "Exercise Increased Caution" — urging travelers to remain alert while visiting the European country.

Known for its medieval cities, historic landmarks, chocolate and beer, Belgium attracts millions of visitors from around the world each year.

AMERICANS WARNED POPULAR TRAVEL ROUTES THIS SUMMER COULD CARRY CRIME AND KIDNAPPING RISKS

The updated advisory warns that petty crime is common, especially in popular tourist areas.

"Most crimes against foreigners are crimes of opportunity, like purse snatching and pickpocketing," the State Department said in its advisory.

Beyond petty crime, the department warned that Belgium remains at risk for terrorist attacks and related activity.

Officials also cautioned that large, generally peaceful demonstrations related to the local political situation can occur and may disrupt transportation and other essential services.

"Stay aware of your surroundings. Stay alert in tourist spots," the advisory states.

The State Department also advises travelers to remain alert around banks and ATMs. It urges that people avoid demonstrations and crowds, and that they monitor local media for breaking news that could affect travel plans.

Before departing, officials recommend that people familiarize themselves with local laws and customs. 

The U.S. Embassy notes that marijuana and other drugs remain illegal in Belgium and warns that bringing drugs into, through or out of the country can result in serious criminal penalties.

The embassy also reminds travelers to keep a close watch on backpacks and small bags, particularly on trains and at major train stations, where thefts can occur.

Fox News Digital reached out to the State Department for comment.

item.title: GOP lawmaker's gifts, 'effusive affection' toward young staffers detailed in explosive ethics report
item.description: The House Ethics Committee recommends censure after an ethics probe found Chuck Edwards violated the code of conduct with two young female staffers.
item.content:encoded:
A House GOP lawmaker is accused of sexually harassing two "young female staffers" in his office in an explosive report that details lavish gifts, trips, and even reciting a poem for one of the aides in an incident that made others in his office uncomfortable.

The House Ethics Committee is recommending a censure for Rep. Chuck Edwards, R-N.C., after an extensive probe found that he violated the House of Representatives' code of conduct with repeated incidents targeting the two staffers.

"Specifically, the Committee found that Representative Edwards engaged in persistent unprofessional and inappropriate conduct towards two young female staffers. While Representative Edwards denied that any of his conduct was intended as a sexual or romantic advance, his pattern of behavior would lead a reasonable observer to interpret it as such, including providing the young women with lavish and recurrent gifts, making comments regarding their appearance and dress, inviting them to intimate dinners and vacations, sending notes regarding his effusive affection, and inviting them to other activities as a way to spend time together," the report said.

The committee also said Edwards sought to cooperate with the panel, but that some messages deemed relevant to the probe were "omitted and/or seemingly deleted from his phone."

REPUBLICAN LAWMAKER WELCOMES HOUSE ETHICS PROBE INTO SEXUAL MISCONDUCT ALLEGATIONS AGAINST HIM

"An example of Representative Edwards’ unprofessional conduct was commenting on the two women’s appearance in the congressional office, telling them when they looked 'pretty' or 'breathtaking,' and even remarking on one staffer’s weight," the report said.

Edwards told the committee he only commented on staffers' clothing and said "it’s almost an insult if you don’t make some comment about [one another’s clothing]," according to the report.

While sexual harassment allegations are detailed regarding both staffers, the report goes into significant detail about Edwards' alleged entreaties to the aide referred to as "Staffer 2."

RESIGNATION IS THE NEW ESCAPE HATCH AS LAWMAKERS FACE EXPULSION

That includes that Edwards "wrote poems for Staffer 2, including one that he read at her going away party in the congressional office accompanied by a slideshow, during which he cried."

"Several staffers present testified that they felt uncomfortable, and Representative Edwards acknowledged in his own testimony that he could tell the staff felt uncomfortable," the report said.

Edwards also "arranged for a singer to go to Staffer 2’s birthday party to sing Ed Sheeran’s Hills of Aberfeldy and say that it was ‘from a special someone,’" according to the findings.

That staffer confided in a friend after the ordeal that it left her "scared lowkey," the report said.

The congressman also went to her home "to perform chores like yard work, pick her up and drop her off for events and activities with his driver."

He also missed House votes to help Staffer 2 decorate her Christmas tree, according to the report.

The findings also state he "Took Staffer 2 to the casino, bought her drinks and paid for her to gamble. Staffer 2 texted Representative Edwards after one such outing to thank him for a fun night."

He printed that text message on paper and drew a heart next to it, the report said, and handwrote, "Perhaps my proudest personal moment!"

Edwards is also accused of booking and paying for spa treatments for that staffer and sending both staffers "personal texts late in the evening."

Later, when "Staffer 2" told Edwards that she received another job offer, Edwards told her he cried and then proceeded to "repeatedly" ask her to dinner for the next several days, the report said.

She told the congressman that it was not "a great idea" after a friend asked her about rumors of an affair between Edwards and a staffer, to which the report said Edwards responded, "It’s disappointing to feel something that used to be easy has gotten complicated. Whether we were talking about cat poop, crime plots, or thoughts more meaningful—I’ve always valued the time we shared, and the money we won :) and I thought you might too. I didn’t expect outside chatter to change that. Still, I understand. You get to set the boundaries, and I get to respect them. If you ever feel easy again, I hope you’ll give me the signal."

Edwards told the committee that he "suppose[d]" his response could seem intended to make someone feel guilty, but that was not his intent.

"That was my way of saying – I ain’t asking again because part of harassment is, when an interaction is not wanted and repetitive, and I was just trying to set the groundwork for ‘I’m going [] to respect that," he apparently told the committee.

Edwards also said the text showed he allowed those staffers to set boundaries on what they were comfortable with, but the committee noted it "received evidence that Staffer 1 and Staffer 2 did not always feel free to reject Representative Edwards’ attentions without fear of professional consequences."

With "Staffer 1," Edwards is also accused of leaving an event early and telling her it was because she "brought a date," but he told the committee "that he told Staffer 1 that he did not want to be ‘in the way or something to that effect.’"

The House Ethics Committee is chaired by Edwards' fellow Republican Rep. Michael Guest, R-Miss., but acts on a bipartisan basis to investigate lawmakers on both sides of the aisle.

The explosive report comes after a string of high-profile sexual harassment allegations against House members including now-former Reps. Eric Swalwell, D-Calif., and Tony Gonzalez, R-Texas, both of whom have since resigned amid the blowback.

item.title: Michigan reports 2 deaths in rare parasite outbreak that has sickened more than 11,000
item.description: Two deaths linked to Michigan's cyclosporiasis outbreak had significant underlying health conditions impacted by the intestinal parasite and dehydration, health officials said.
item.content:encoded:
Two people in Michigan have died in connection with the state's sprawling cyclosporiasis outbreak, marking a rare fatal outcome from the intestinal parasite, health officials said Monday.

The Michigan Department of Health and Human Services (MDHHS) said the deaths were identified as part of the ongoing outbreak, which has so far sickened 11,234 people statewide. As of Thursday, 193 people with reported infections said they had been hospitalized.

According to the agency, medical records showed both people who died "had significant underlying health conditions that may have been impacted by cyclosporiasis and dehydration." Officials said no additional information about the cases will be released.

CYCLOSPORA OUTBREAK: IS IT STILL SAFE TO EAT AT RESTAURANTS? HERE'S WHAT TO KNOW

State health officials are continuing to investigate the source of the outbreak and said available evidence points to lettuce or salad greens as a potential culprit. However, investigators cautioned that other food items have not been ruled out, and no specific type of produce, grower or supplier has been identified.

MDHHS said it is working with local health departments and other partners as the investigation continues and will provide updates as more information becomes available.

WHITE HOUSE ADDRESSES GROWING PARASITE OUTBREAK AFTER MORE THAN 400 AMERICANS SICKENED

Cyclosporiasis is an intestinal illness caused by the parasite Cyclospora cayetanensis. The hallmark symptom of a cyclospora infection is watery, often "explosive" diarrhea that can last for weeks or even months if left untreated, the CDC says. Other symptoms include severe abdominal cramping, bloating, nausea, fatigue and significant weight loss.

Health officials emphasized that cyclosporiasis is generally not considered a life-threatening illness and that deaths associated with the infection are uncommon in the United States.

Fox News Digital's Angelica Stabile contributed to this report.

item.title: Trump DOJ corners school district with 7-day ultimatum over trans policy keeping parents in the dark
item.description: Harmeet Dhillon demands Anne Arundel County Public Schools stop hiding student gender identity information from parents or face DOJ litigation.
item.content:encoded:
Assistant Attorney General Harmeet Dhillon demanded in a letter sent July 29 that a school district in Maryland stop hiding information about student gender transitions from parents or face litigation from the Justice Department.

"By categorically withholding ‘(i)nformation about a student’s gender identity’ from parents except where ‘legally required,’ AACPS appears to have adopted a blanket, district-wide practice of nondisclosure untethered to FERPA’s enumerated exceptions … parents were denied access to their child’s full record, information was disclosed without parental consent, and the parents were denied a hearing to correct the record," she wrote, aimed at the Anne Arundel County school system. 

"Comply with the law or face us in court," Dhillon later added on X.

The demand marks the Trump administration’s latest effort to challenge school policies that allow students to socially transition without their parents’ knowledge, testing whether federal education privacy law requires districts to disclose gender-identity records. Anne Arundel County now faces possible litigation — and potentially the loss of federal funding — unless it reverses the policy within seven days, escalating a national dispute over parental rights, a significant plank in the president's policy agenda.

'SHAME ON YOU': SHERRILL KNEW VOTER-ROLL BOMBSHELL WAS COMING WHEN SHE CALLED TRUMP A LIAR, DOJ OFFICIAL SAYS

The Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA) is designed to give parents the legal right to access their children’s educational records, which the Trump administration argues includes information related to changes in their gender identity. The law has previously been used by the DOJ in attempts to overturn similar policies in Maine and California.

LGBT advocates argue that nondisclosure for information linked to a child’s gender identity is important to preserving the safety of children growing up in non-affirming or abusive households. Social conservatives, meanwhile, take the position that schools don’t have the right to conceal information about their children from them.

Before Dhillon sent her letter Wednesday, the DOJ and the Department of Education announced that they had entered a partnership to crack down on transgender nondisclosure policies in both Anne Arundel County and Ann Arbor Public Schools in Michigan, potentially withholding federal funds from the district until it changes course.

VIRGINIA SCHOOL DISTRICT SUED OVER ALLEGED POLICY OF KEEPING STUDENTS' GENDER TRANSITIONS HIDDEN FROM PARENTS

In a press release announcing the joint effort, the agencies claimed that the Education Department had received complaints from parents in Anne Arundel County who alleged the district "was secretly helping their daughter pretend to be male at school" and declined to provide information about it when confronted.

An Education Department official told Fox News Digital that the agency does not comment on ongoing investigations and a DOJ spokesperson referred Fox News Digital to Dhillon's remarks when reached for comment.

Students enrolled in Anne Arundel Public Schools are, per district policy, allowed to use any name or pronoun they prefer, even if it doesn’t align with their sex, without requiring parental approval. Staff are, however, instructed to involve the student’s family in developing a support plan for the student unless "there is a genuine safety concern for the student’s physical, emotional, or mental health safety."

TRUMP ADMINISTRATION OPENS FOUR TITLE IX INVESTIGATIONS INTO MICHIGAN AND NORTH CAROLINA SCHOOL DISTRICTS

Additionally, the policy designates records about student gender identity as confidential medical information and advises that it should be revealed when legally necessary.

The Anne Arundel, Maryland, and Ann Arbor, Michigan, school districts did not respond to requests for comment when reached by Fox News Digital.

"School districts that hide information from parents are violating federal law," Dhillon said. "FERPA is not optional, and any districts that attempt to bypass or distort its requirements should expect immediate federal action. In partnership with the Department of Education, the Department of Justice will initiate enforcement proceedings with districts that fail to comply."

Dhillon's letter gives Anne Arundel Public Schools seven days to rescind its policy, provide parents impacted with the relevant records and inform staff that they cannot withhold information from parents. If the deadline is not met, the letter claims the district could face legal action.

"In your view, rank the top three most effective presidents in American history," Marc Morial, the president of the National Urban League, asked Harris at the National Urban League conference on Friday.

She joked, "Marc, don't make me do that."

Harris then went on to name Franklin Delano Roosevelt (FDR) as her first pick and said she watched an NPR special about him recently.

KAMALA HARRIS IS THE 'FAIRLY OBVIOUS' 2028 PRESIDENTIAL FRONTRUNNER, DEMOCRATIC INSIDERS SAY

"It was he who talked about the expansion of the Supreme Court, and then he got ferocious back — kind of blowback for that. But he did good. It was Social Security. It was, you know, when I think about what he did in terms of investing in the people in during dire times and talking about the role and responsibility of government, that it should not just be about the benevolence of community organizations or just interpersonal relationships, that the government has a role. I think that he was a very important president," she said.

She went on to name John F. Kennedy — also noting Lyndon B. Johnson, Kennedy's vice president, who took over the presidency after he was assassinated.

"I credit, you know, Kennedy, of course, in terms of what he laid the groundwork for and then Johnson followed up on," she said. "Around having the ability, but that was again an example of the inside outside game. Because the reason that happened is because the pressure was on from the outside to appeal to the conscience of the people on the inside."

HILLARY CLINTON STILL FUMING OVER ELECTORAL COLLEGE, CALLS IT AN 'ABOMINATION' IN NEW NETFLIX SERIES

Harris listed Barack Obama as her third choice, which the audience applauded.

"What he did with the Affordable Care Act among many things, but in particular, if we had one issue that has been ailing America for generations, which is a healthcare system that has failed anyone other than the rich and addressing that the way that he did and took a lot of heat for it. I think it's one of the greatest presidents," Harris said.

The list notably left off Biden, under whom she served as vice president.

Neither Harris' office nor Biden's office immediately returned Fox News Digital's requests for comment.

Harris took Biden's spot at the top of the Democratic presidential ticket in 2024 after the former president decided to exit the race following a rough debate performance against now-President Donald Trump.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Harris had a little over 100 days to mount a presidential campaign, and wrote in her book after the election that his decision to run for a second term was reckless. 

"'It’s Joe and Jill’s decision.' We all said that, like a mantra, as if we’d all been hypnotized. Was it grace, or was it recklessness?" Harris wrote. "In retrospect, I think it was recklessness. The stakes were simply too high. This wasn’t a choice that should have been left to an individual’s ego, an individual’s ambition. It should have been more than a personal decision."

Harris took a series of left-wing policy positions during the conversation, and said she had not made a decision about 2028 yet.

"We must allow for a real conversation about revisiting certain things," Harris said. "I know this is gonna be controversial coming from me, in particular. We need to revisit the Electoral College."

Harris lost both the Electoral College and the popular vote to President Donald Trump in the 2024 election.

She also voiced support for expanding the Supreme Court.

"We need to revisit the point of expanding the court to 13 justices, like we have 13 district courts," Harris said. She also suggested the U.S. should revisit statehood for Puerto Rico, expanding beyond her previous support for statehood for Washington, D.C.

Zeteo founder and far-left commentator Mehdi Hasan reacted to a clip posted of Harris with a Biden animation where he appeared surprised.

The Independent's Eric Michael Garcia also reacted with a gif of the former president.

item.title: USMNT agree to new contract with coach Mauricio Pochettino through 2030 World Cup as obvious theme emerges
item.description: Mauricio Pochettino agreed to a new contract to manage the USMNT through the 2030 World Cup after leading the team to its first knockout win since 2002.
item.content:encoded:
Familiarity will be a theme for the U.S. men's national soccer team at the 2030 World Cup.

Despite major speculation before and throughout the 2026 World Cup that manager Mauricio Pochettino was leaning toward returning to the club level, the United States Soccer Federation announced Monday that the 54-year-old had agreed to a new contract to keep him on the red, white, and blue sideline through 2030.

"Working together with U.S. Soccer over the past two years, it has become clear to us that there is tremendous potential to make the Men’s National Team program even stronger," Pochettino said in the announcement.

LANDON DONOVAN SAYS SOCCER HAS ARRIVED IN AMERICA AFTER RECORD-BREAKING WORLD CUP SUMMER

"The passion we experienced from the fans throughout the World Cup only strengthened our belief in what is possible here. We are excited by the opportunity to bring all our experience and knowledge to even more areas of U.S. Soccer while helping strengthen the pathways for players, coaches and teams across the Federation. We want to try to have a lasting impact on the sport in the country that has welcomed us so warmly and for that impact to extend beyond results on the field."

Pochettino and staff led the USMNT to just its third World Cup group stage outright win in team history at the 2026 World Cup, as well as the squad's first knockout-stage win since 2002 with a 2-0 win over Bosnia and Herzegovina.

TAYLOR TWELLMAN GOES OFF ON TEAM USA AFTER DISASTROUS 4-1 LOSS TO BELGIUM: 'CAN'T MISS FUNDAMENTALS'

The USMNT was certainly looking to earn a spot in the quarterfinals, at minimum, in Pochettino's first run as World Cup manager, and while it fell short thanks to a wildly disappointing outing against Belgium in the Round of 16, it's difficult to say his re-upping with the national team is not a significant win for American soccer.

On paper, that is, at the very least.

For starters, it's hard to imagine the USMNT attracting a bigger, more-proven name than Pochettino to take over. On top of that, USA soccer presumably handing over more rein to a proven manager trying to build a team culture while the country continues to grow its own soccer culture feels like a no-brainer.

The 2030 World Cup will be jointly hosted by Portugal, Spain, and Morocco.

It is impossible to predict what the USMNT will look like in four years, but having the same manager building momentum who is already familiar with the territory, players, and prospects is a great first for the future of American soccer.

item.title: Softball hall of famer sends blunt warning to those defending inclusion of biological males in female sports

MARTINA NAVRATILOVA SAYS BILLIE JEAN KING’S TRANS-ATHLETE STANCE ‘DOESN’T SQUARE’ WITH HER OWN WORDS

MEGAN RAPINOE SAYS EFFORTS TO BAR TRANS ATHLETES FROM WOMEN'S SPORTS ARE 'ATTACK ON WOMEN IN SOCIETY'

item.title: Top Dem torches socialists taking over his party: 'They're anti-American'
item.description: Josh Gottheimer says Democratic Socialists of America are "not Democrats" and accuses them of trying to hijack the party as a vessel for socialism.
item.content:encoded:
A leading House Democrat went scorched-earth on insurgent socialists rising within his party, repeatedly telling them to start their own party and accusing them of trying to "hijack" the Democratic Party as a "vessel" for their communist, "anti-American," open-border platform.

House Intelligence Committee member Josh Gottheimer, D-N.J., a leader of the moderate Blue Dog Coalition, told Fox News on Sunday that the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) is "not Democrats" and rejected the idea that its platform is compatible with the Democratic Party’s.

"Obviously, I'm a very proud, commonsense Democrat, and I don't think DSA members are Democrats. They're socialists, right? And I'm all for them having their own party if they want one, but if they're trying to take over our party, that's unacceptable to me," Gottheimer said on "The Big Weekend Show."

DEM REP HENRY CUELLAR REJECTS DSA AGENDA, SAYS SOCIALISTS ARE TRYING TO 'USE' DEMOCRATIC PARTY

"Their values, their ideas are certainly not in line with ours, and they don't support our leadership. They're trying to use the Democratic Party as a vessel for their ideas. And as you heard in some of these conventions, literally, they're supporting the Communist Manifesto and [Leon] Trotsky, they're anti-American, they are anti-cop, they don't believe in borders."

Gottheimer was referring to man-on-the-street clips of DSA members at the group’s Chicago convention. One socialist said they are organizing a front to get "ICE off our campuses," while a member of the DSA’s National Political Committee said people such as Gottheimer who call them anti-American do not understand that their platform is the "most American thing you can do."

Another DSA NPC member said socialism is the "same kind of stuff that I am used to [in] growing up in the Christian Church."

DEMOCRATIC SOCIALISTS OF AMERICA ACTIVISTS SIGNED PLEDGE TO SUPPORT, DEFEND 'CHINESE SOCIALISM'

Gottheimer said 45 million voters are registered Democrats, compared with 150,000 official DSA members.

"They’re not welcome in the Democratic Party," he said.

He pushed back against members of his own party who have expressed openness to DSA-aligned candidates such as Maine oysterman Graham Platner.

GRAHAM PLATNER BLAMES NAZI TATTOO ON MILITARY ‘CULTURE,’ DRAWS BACKLASH FROM GOP VETERANS

Rep. Ro Khanna, D-Calif., who represents Silicon Valley, said Democrats should not have "watched wealth pile up on Wall Street and Silicon Valley" at the expense of working-class Americans, adding that "the Democratic Party needs reform."

Gottheimer countered that fringe coalitions are mounting insurgencies in both parties and "trying to barge in" with incompatible ideas.

He also pointed to longtime Clinton confidant James Carville, who told Fox News that he would disown the Democratic Party if left-wing streamer Hasan Piker were permitted to become one of its leaders.

Former U.S. Marine Corps bomb technician Johnny Joey Jones asked whether Gottheimer would also leave the party over Piker or if Democratic leaders embraced socialists such as Harlem’s Darializa Chevalier.

"Well, [House Minority Leader Hakeem] Jeffries won’t — and let me be very clear that Hasan Piker is not a Democrat – the guy is the ultimate grifter, right? He’s the guy who said that 9/11 is America’s fault… We’ve got to make it clear he’s not welcome in the Democratic Party."

Gottheimer said the DSA platform shows that the organization is incompatible with the Democratic Party. He added that socialists can "scream and yell and try to …hijack [the party] and shove their ideas in and use it as a vessel."

"We have to make clear that’s not who we are…"

While Gottheimer reiterated that he does not plan to leave the Democratic Party any time soon, Jones noted that one prominent New Jersey Democrat already has.

Rep. Jeff Van Drew, whose district includes Cape May, switched parties during President Donald Trump’s first term, angering South Jersey Democratic committees as the longtime lawmaker embraced Trump’s platform.

"You wouldn't be the first New Jersey congressman to find a better party. I'm just saying leave the door open if you want to," Jones said.

Gottheimer’s district includes liberal New York City suburbs immediately west of the George Washington Bridge and the deep-red, Trump-friendly Skylands near the Delaware Water Gap, making it one of the most politically diverse districts in the state’s congressional delegation.

Fox News Digital reached out to the DSA and Piker for comment.
